title: Limit Your Inputs
coreMove: Stillness grows when you choose which inputs may enter and when; scheduled email, muted alerts, and delayed news protect judgment from borrowed urgency.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who feel guilty delaying low-stakes inputs
exampleSpecs.stakes: a meeting may waste attention on demands that time would sort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Set up expected harm from delay, then reveal that waiting sorted the inputs.

exampleSpecs.audience: workers whose chats and alerts keep taking over planned work
exampleSpecs.stakes: a quote may be late because every channel claims the morning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use a compressed message exchange to show an access rule.

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose first work block gets split by phone alerts
exampleSpecs.stakes: the first paragraph may inherit the mood of the alerts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A worker changes the work surface before alerts can choose the first paragraph.

exampleSpecs.audience: operators who want a physical handle for incoming paper
exampleSpecs.stakes: morning judgment can be spent by whichever envelope sits on top
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A small desk detail makes delay visible without a live decision.

exampleSpecs.audience: teams reviewing a communication failure after the fact
exampleSpecs.stakes: a false line reached customers because noise sat beside the draft
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist catches an unverified line before it reaches customers.

exampleSpecs.audience: workers who notice their own inbox error midstream
exampleSpecs.stakes: a forecast may be late because reply momentum feels like work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A compressed exchange shows a worker refusing reply momentum until the forecast is named.
